title: The Legion controller becomes a live terminal session and merges pull requests itself

spec.status: Every requirement, acceptance criterion, error behaviour, and rejected alternative in the spec is settled. This plan implements it; it does not reopen any of it.

tree: Single issue, one PR, no children. Phases: planner (this) -> implementer -> tester -> reviewer -> merger.

branch.name: legion/LEGION-16
branch.baseAtPlanTime: 7db2cd83 (chore: release cli v1.1.2); main@origin was b24f8e79 (pi-envoy v1.4.2 release, version bump only). Rebase onto current main before opening the PR if anything under packages/ or skills/ moved.
branch.workspaceRule: Every shell command starts `cd -- "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" &&`; every jj command uses `-R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE"`.

summary: Ten ordered tasks. Contracts first (T1) because the daemon routes (T3-T5) and the pi-envoy extension (T7) both compile against @legion/contracts. Then state schema + migration (T2), the daemon process change (T3), the two daemon route slices (T4 ready/ompSessionFile, T5 grants/merge authority), the CLI (T6), the addressing fragment (T7), the extension (T8), the pr-queue retirement + controller skill (T9), docs (T10), and the PR body + tester handoff (T11). Each task names its files, symbols, observable acceptance, and the test that proves it. The `contradictions` list records where current code disagrees with the spec so the implementer does not rediscover it.
globalConstraints: Repo conventions: Biome (double quotes, semicolons, 100 cols), strict TS, `node:` imports, `type` imports, no barrel files, co-located `__tests__/`, Bun test. Run `bunx biome check`, `bunx tsc --noEmit`, `bun test`, and `go test ./...` (in packages/envoy) once at the end, not per task.
jj, not git: `jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" new` per logical commit; never `jj abandon`, `jj edit @-`, or `jj op restore`. Commit attribution is automatic.
Only the implementer creates the bookmark and PR: `jj bookmark set legion/LEGION-16 && jj git push --bookmark legion/LEGION-16`, then `legion gh -- pr create` with `Dispatch: LEGION-16` in the body.
No `docs/plans/` file for this issue. `.legion/plan.json` is the only plan artifact (spec Acceptance 6).
Tests are permanent load: keep a test only where a plausible bug would fail it; delete tests that pin the shim/socket behaviour this change removes rather than re-pinning them to new text.
Existing tests that assert `addressingFragment(...)` by calling the function (processes.test.ts lines 634, 1513, 2206, 2237, 5647) self-adjust; only literal-text assertions need editing.

rigNotes.source: docs/solutions/legion/worker-pane-shell-gotchas.md (read it first; none of these is in scope to fix here)
rigNotes.stackedGrants: The pi-envoy bash hook prepends N `export LEGION_GRANT=` blocks per call and only the first redeems. Source the `export`-shadowing function from that doc's section 1 once per session and end every grant-consuming command (`jj git push`, `legion gh`, `legion handoff complete`) with `; grant_release`. Grants expire 60 seconds after mint (GRANT_TTL_MS in api.ts), so run the consuming command in the same bash call that minted it.
rigNotes.daemonTestSuiteInAPane: Every Legion pane carries DISPATCH_URL/DISPATCH_TOKEN_FILE, which makes one pre-existing CLI test (`legion start --check-config > validates github_apps.<role>.private_key_command...`) fail only inside a pane. Run `env -u DISPATCH_URL -u DISPATCH_TOKEN_FILE bun test` and say so in the handoff; CI is unaffected.
rigNotes.jjSplitBookmark: After `jj split -m '...' <paths>` the issue bookmark stays on the empty working copy; before every push run `jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" bookmark set legion/LEGION-16 -r @- --allow-backwards` then `jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" git push --bookmark legion/LEGION-16`, after checking `jj diff -r @- --stat` holds exactly the intended paths.

constraintB_plainLanguageForHumans.appliesTo: Anything a human reads: the PR title and body (including the `## Verification` block's prose), every dispatch_message and dispatch_comment, every GitHub PR comment or review this issue's workers post.
constraintB_plainLanguageForHumans.rule: Full sentences in plain English, one idea per sentence. No repo shorthand or coined nouns. Expand every identifier on first use: an issue key gets its title, a PR number gets its title, a file gets what it is for, a symbol gets what it does. No bare event ids. The `.legion/*.json` handoffs are machine-read and exempt.

contradictions.current: Both `delete this.deps.state.controllerLocator` when the pane is dead or being retired. `ensureController` (1396-1418) calls `controllerAlive()` FIRST and only then `spawnController(secret)`, so by the time the respawn runs the locator, and with it any recorded `ompSessionFile`, is already gone.
contradictions.spec: Errors table: `controller pane dead on probe -> ensureController respawns with --resume when a session file is recorded`.
contradictions.resolution: T3 captures `const resumeSessionFile = this.deps.state.controllerLocator?.ompSessionFile` at the top of `ensureController`, before the probe, and passes it to `spawnController(secret, resumeSessionFile)`; `spawnController` writes it onto the fresh locator (mirroring `launchWorker` lines 2508-2509) so a `/controller/ready` that omits the field does not lose it. `retireAndRespawnStuckController` stops deleting the locator itself: it kills the pane and calls `ensureController()`, whose own probe then finds the pane dead, clears the locator, and resumes.

contradictions.where: packages/daemon/src/daemon/api/auth.ts `Grant` (13-18), `SessionCapability` (6-11); api/github.ts `appRoleForLegionRole(role: LegionRole)` (16-18); contracts `Grant.request` (legion-daemon-api.ts 221-229, strictObject requiring tree+issue); `LEGION_ROLES` excludes `controller`
contradictions.current: A grant's `role` is always a `LegionRole` copied from a `SessionCapability`; the controller never has a `SessionCapability` (only `state.controllerCapabilityHash`, checked by `requireController`), so it cannot reach `/grants` at all, and `appRoleForLegionRole("controller")` does not type-check.
contradictions.spec: `/grants` accepts `{secret, sessionId}` authenticated by the controller capability and mints `role: "controller"`; `appRoleForLegionRole("controller") -> implement`.
contradictions.resolution: T5 widens `Grant` to a two-member union and adds the controller branch to `handleGrants`, following the dual-credential precedent in `api/routes/issues.ts` `handleIssueStatus` (lines 23-55: presence of both optional fields selects the session form; neither selects the controller form; exactly one is 400). Do NOT put `controller` into `LEGION_ROLES` (it is not a phase role; `roleToken`/`parseRoleToken` would accept it).

contradictions.current: Reads `grant.issue` and `grant.role` and calls `roleToken(project, grant.issue, grant.role)`; a controller grant has no issue and is not a phase.
contradictions.resolution: T5: after `resolveGrant`, `if (grant.role === "controller") throw new HttpError(403, "A controller grant cannot complete a phase")` — this also narrows the union for the rest of the handler.

contradictions.current: The live LEGION deployment's controller predates this change and holds no merge credential, so it cannot merge PR LEGION-16 itself.
contradictions.resolution: Not an implementer item. The merger for this issue publishes READY as usual; if the controller topic has no capable holder, it follows the 404 fallback to the architect, and the architect surfaces the READY to Sami with `dispatch_message` for a one-time human merge (spec Design, Bootstrap). Recorded here so nobody treats it as a defect.

planDecisions.decision: `ensureController` carries the resume file across the liveness probe (see C1). `spawnController(controllerSecret, resumeSessionFile?)` calls the existing `computeResumeArgument(issue, resumeSessionFile, logVerb)` (processes.ts 1995-2020) so a recorded-but-missing session file throws (same-agent invariant, same as roots/workers) and a recorded file logs `[legion] <logVerb> <label> by resuming OMP session <file>`. `computeResumeArgument`'s first parameter is typed `IssueKey` (= `string`, contracts/legion-roles.ts:8) and is used only in log text, so pass `controllerToken(project)` as the label and `"resurrecting the controller"` as the verb.
planDecisions.why: Boring reuse over a parallel helper; the only alternative (a separate persisted `controllerResumeSessionFile`) is a second state field for one consumer.

planDecisions.decision: `/controller/ready` stores `ompSessionFile` only when `state.controllerLocator` exists; otherwise it logs `[legion] controller/ready reported an OMP session file but no controller pane is recorded; a later respawn cannot resume it` and continues.
planDecisions.why: A `/legion-claim-controller` from a hand-started session has no daemon pane to resume into; the daemon must not invent a locator.

planDecisions.decision: The controller grant form does not additionally require `sessionId` to equal `state.roles[controllerToken].sessionId`; `sessionId` is recorded on the grant so `deleteCapability(sessionId)` semantics stay uniform.
planDecisions.why: The controller secret is a single 0600-file capability held only by the controller pane; the spec's error table defines only the wrong-secret failure. Adding a second check invents a rule the spec does not have.

planDecisions.decision: Daemon 403 text for a non-controller grant with `merge: true`: `Only the controller may merge; publish READY to the controller`. CLI `CliError` message: `this grant cannot merge; publish READY to the controller` followed by `: <daemon error text>` when the response body parses as `{error}`.
planDecisions.why: Spec names the CLI phrase; appending the daemon's reason keeps an expired-grant 403 distinguishable from the authority refusal.

planDecisions.decision: The merger's READY message carries the issue key and the PR URL alongside `READY #<n> at <sha>` and the gate facts, e.g. first line `READY #<n> at <sha> for <KEY> (<pr url>)`. The controller resolves the tree's architect topic as `notifications.role.` + `legion-<project>-<root>-architect` using `legion state --json` (`issues[<KEY>].parent` chain to the root, or `trees`).
planDecisions.why: The controller must reply to the tree's architect (spec Errors table); without the issue key in the message it cannot find that topic. The addressing fragment gives the merger the controller topic; nothing gives the controller the architect topic except state.

planDecisions.decision: A READY that cannot merge yet only because required checks are still running, a flake rerun was issued, or `mergeable == UNKNOWN` is a *pending READY*: the controller `envoy_subscribe`s to `notifications.github.<owner>.<repo>.pr.<n>.checks` (and `pr.<n>` lifecycle), re-verifies on that wake using the READY sha from its own conversation, and `envoy_unsubscribe`s once it has merged or reported a failed gate. If a resumed controller no longer has the READY in context, it asks the merger's role topic (from the wake's `source_session`/issue key) to republish READY rather than guessing a sha.
planDecisions.why: Spec: the controller never polls; `pr.<n>.checks` is the wake. The daemon routes PR events to the architect, not the controller, so the controller must subscribe itself. Conversation memory is the controller's only state (`Controller state is disposable` forbids local bookkeeping, not remembering the current wake).

planDecisions.decision: `retireAndRespawnStuckController` passes `{ skipGraceful: true }` to `stopProcess`; `stopProcess`'s parameter type drops `socketPath` for the controller call site only via the existing structural type (no signature change needed: `socketPath?` stays for workers).
planDecisions.why: Spec: controller stop paths use the pane-kill branch. Explicit is clearer than relying on `locator.socketPath` being undefined.
